Spy vs Spy commissioned

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The Spy Cables dominated news headlines this week. But the one unanswered question at this stage is who leaked all the documents and why?

Summary:
South Africa entered it's own Wiki-leaks era this week, with Al Jazeera starting to publish thousands of classified security documents from our intelligence agency that was somehow leaked to them.
We will start the story with a short overview of intelligence history in SA leading up to the 1994 change of government, explaining how South Africa started playing a very dangerous diplomatic game, trying to be friends with countries who are traditional foes. We will also look at internal tensions in the ruling party and also between the foreign and domestic legs of our newly merged NIA.
As a twist in the tail we will be interviewing a former head of NIA stating that the information was not leaked but hacked by international hackers with an agenda on the middle east.

Further information:
We wil follow the theory of international hacking by interviewing 3 characters around this issue. Richard Poplak from Daily maverick explains why he thinks Israel did it. Jasmine Opperman (ex-NIA) and a Trac vetted cyber terorism expert from Washington DC both puts the argument forward that Iran is responsible for the leak.

Extra Budget Items:
Derek and Richard Davies were on standby for a third day on GM's request for interview wit minister.
3 hours of landline call to Washington DC

Ms. Jasmine Opperman Director Africa TRAC
Mr. Richard Poplak Journalist for The Daily Maverick

Press Release:


Spy Cables
The leak of hundreds of highly classified State Security Agency documents has placed South Africa on a diplomatic knife-edge. The explosive contents finger SA as a halfway-house for terror groups and highlight the State’s alleged inability to secure classified information. Who might have leaked these documents? And, why? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Final Version



Studio link
This week the so-called “Spy-cables” made headlines around the world. 1000's of documents from our State Security Agency, or SSA, were leaked to Al Jazeera and The Guardian, and on Monday they started releasing them bit by bit, giving us a glimpse into the real world of dirty politics and the wars which play out beneath the radar of everyday life.

Script:

A military plane flies over the City of Tshwane, or Pretoria on an overcast morning this week. For many of the city’s residents everything suddenly looks suspicious, as South Africa faces the biggest leak of its top secret security and intelligence documents in history. Also, because the leak is an uncomfortable reminder that there is a parallel reality away from elections and parliamentary brawls where the clandestine decisions made, impact all of our lives.

A military plane flies over the City of Tshwane, or Pretoria on an overcast morning this week. Our Capital city’s residents are reeling following the biggest leak of top secret security and intelligence documents in South African history. This leak is an uncomfortable reminder of a clandestine parallel reality - away from elections and parliamentary brawls – in which covert decisions made behind closed doors, affect us all.
Derek link
The very name of Pretoria has been under threat for some time. And now it's been dubbed the “Eldorado of Espionage”, literally oozing secrets.

Richard Poplak, an award winning journalist for the Daily Maverick, has been following the story closely.
Richard Polack
We are talking about almost 150 individuals who are registered, working on espionage activity. So, everybody's watching everybody. And this is what we mean when we say the deep state. This is the deep state, it's the state beneath the state, interacting with other states on a level that citizens in a democracy, democracies all over the world, are just completely unaware of.

Instead of the documents being released in one go, we saw them exposed little by little with new cables published daily. Have they been carefully selected for a specific reason? Some revolve around minor local issues, but the attention-grabbing ones deal mostly with Israel and its old foe Iran. Many of the documents are communiqués between our State Security Agency, the SSA and others such as the CIA, Britain’s MI6 and Israel’s Mossad. A number of cables show that while we are dependent on the Iranians for about 40% of our oil imports, and have numerous bilateral trade agreements with them, we have in fact been spying on them all along.

Jasmin Opperman, who worked for our then National Intelligence Agency, the NIA, is now the African Director of a subscription based organisation with experts all over the globe who study and analyse Terrorism threats and trends
Jasmine
There has been for example a document on iran, where we had an Operational Target Analysis, – that's the heart of intelligence work. Your target analysis sets your whole process. To get to a point of target analysis there has to be certain processes informing the justification of you going to work on a target. That process is built on a principle of accountability. Why am I doing this investigation. There will be serious questions asked because intelligence will have to stand up now and say on what basis have certain investigations been conducted.

But, perhaps because the documents may have been published selectively, Iran seems for the most part to come out clean while Israel seems to be seen getting its hands dirty. One cable indicates that Mossad offered to return a blueprint for a missile system stolen from South Africa. Another document describes a Mossad agent as extremely arrogant.
Derek – driving link about Carte Blanche story
Carte Blanche also features in the spy cables saga, a story we did at OR Tambo, about five years ago.
Carte blanche insert
We exposed Israeli agents, posing as security guards for Israeli airline El-Al, even carrying fire arms and with access to all areas of the airport, spying on whoever they pleased.
INSERT SOUNDUP
We're security from the airport here. You're not flying today? You're from airport security? Yes. Airport security? No they are not, says Jonathan garb, a former El Al security employee. This here is secret service operating above the law in South Africa. We pull the wool over every one's eyes. We do exactly what we want, the local authorities do not know what we are doing.

The more documents published this week, the more it was asked how and why they were leaked? Many experts seem to agree that this was a deliberate internal leak from a South African who had access to the files – possibly a disgruntled employee with an axe to grind

Na-eem Jeenah, of the Afro-Middle East Centre says that internal power struggles could have played a part
Na'eem
The third option is some kind of a factional dispute, within the ANC, playing out through the SSA, uhm, that there’s one faction who wants to embarrass the other. One way of doing it is to get this stuff out.

But there is also the possibility that it was not an internal leak. The fact that the most important documents released up to now deal with the Middle East and also that they were not leaked to local media may suggest that the SSA system was hacked by someone with a global agenda. An American expert in cyber terrorism - vetted by Trac and who must remain anonymous - says that this is most likely what happened.
James
The other option is that it is an Advanced Persistent Threat. Some nation state actor or some criminal enterprise that has connections to a nation state actor. If it is a hack, who would be able to break into the system so long, over a number of years? In terms of the countries involved in this actual issue, we have South Africa, Israel and Iran. Both israel and Iran could have done it. Would you like to name your prime suspect? The most sensible source for this, seems to be Iran.
Derek and Richard Poplak
Richard Poplak also suspects a foreign country, but not Iran

It is our contention that the leak originated in Jerusalem. It looks to be like it might have come out of an israeli source, and it was leaked to Al jazeera and The Guardian, primarily to deal with a situation between the civilian politicians in Israel and the intelligence community.

But Jasmine feels that it couldn't be Jerusalem, because they wouldn't inflict so much damage on themselves to settle internal policy disputes.
Jasmine
If one looks at American, Iran relations at this point in time, the delicate balance, and how that relates to the whole issue of stability in the Middle East, and the combat against the islamic State, Isis, the one issue for me that stands out is the name Iran.

But why would Iran run the risk of damaging their relationship with South Africa by releasing these documents?
jasmine
They would sell South Africa down the river, because they have more to gain from their foreign interactions with America, than from South Africa. That is power politics. This is real politics we are talking about.

Iran is struggling under sanctions. whereas Israel is pushing for more sanctions and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has told the UN that Iran will soon have nuclear arms capability.
Upsound: This is a bomb
On the other hand, the US is trying to get out of the war zone in the Middle East. Therefore the democrats under President Obama may be ready to loosen sanctions on Iran, as they need them to help fight Isis.
James
A war of choice, in Iraq, where we poured a trillion dollars in and five or six thousand of our troop's lives into something that was fake. They had no yellow cake, we found no weapons of mass destruction, and the US, politically were exhausted. We're out of Afghanistan now, well for the most part, and we don't want to be dragged back into another mess. You know, being stuck in the middle of someone else's civil war.

But the Republicans who control Congress are historically on the side of Israel. They have now invited Netanyahu to address congress against President Obama’s wishes, and by releasing the leaked documents just before his speech to congress next week, they are showing that even Netanyahu’s own Mossad disagrees with him about Iran’s nuclear capability.

Plausible as this may seem, without proof it remains a theory, and in the mean time, here at home, we have other more pressing concerns about the leaks.
Derek link
We may never know the answer to this whodunnit, but the more important questions remain. What will happen to the documents that haven't been leaked yet, and are our state computers still being hacked?

Securing the system and finding any internal leaks will be costly and time consuming. And, how much damage the leaks have done to our relationship with countries who are surprised that we may be spying on them, remains to be seen. All that is certain is that the media has glimpsed the parallel intelligence reality.
Richard
Think of a pit of snakes, all slithering over each other, and that's what the global geo-political situation looks like. It's our job to try and untangle all of this but it's very difficult when we don't have access to cables like these ones. And that's again what makes cables like these spy cables so fascinating. We're actually able to get into the snake-pit, and try and separate some of these serpents from one another and see what they're all doing. So it absolutely relates to serve a larger African project, where we can try and interpret what's happening on this continent.
